newsitem.title: UK: British Gas extends loss on Capel comment.
newsitem.headline: British Gas extends loss on Capel comment.

text.p: Shares in British Gas Plc extended their earlier losses as analysts at HSBC James Capel considered reassessing their positive stance on the stock, market sources said on Wednesday.
The stock was down 9p at 222 by 1030 GMT in heavy volume of 10.8 million shares -- making the most active stock in the London market.
Analysts at Capel were not immediately available for comment.
Earlier British Gas shares dropped on reports that Royal Dutch/Shell had ruled out a bid for the company, coupled with measures in yesterday's UK budget seen as negative for UK utilities.

The stock was also hit by comment in the Financial Times Lex column that British Gas may come under closer regulatory scrutiny after National Grid Plc delivered higher cost savings than it had told its regulator were achievable.
The decline in Gas shares came after a sharp rise earlier this month on talk of a bid from Shell. After ending October at 190-1/2p, they leapt to a 235-1/2 close on November 25.
